title: Points, Lines, and Angles: Geometry's Atoms

questions.question: How many lines pass through two distinct given points?
questions.rationale: Through any two distinct points there passes exactly one line — a foundational fact used throughout geometry.

questions.question: An angle measuring exactly 90° is called:
questions.rationale: Right angles measure 90°; acute are smaller, obtuse between 90° and 180°, reflex beyond 180°.

questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. Its co-interior partner measures:
questions.rationale: Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to 180°, so the partner is 110°.

questions.question: The angle sum of any triangle is:
questions.rationale: Drawing a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side transfers the interior angles onto a straight line: 180° total.

questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle equals:
options: Half the sum of all angles
The sum of the two remote interior angles
questions.rationale: Exterior angle theorem: it is supplementary to its adjacent interior angle, hence equal to the other two combined.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a ray and a segment?
options: A ray has no starting point; a segment does
A ray extends forever in one direction from an endpoint, while a segment joins two endpoints with measurable length
A segment extends forever in both directions
questions.rationale: A ray starts at a point and goes on forever in one direction; a segment is bounded by two endpoints and therefore has a measurable length.

questions.question: The angles around a single point sum to:
questions.rationale: Angles meeting at a point complete a full turn: they sum to 360° (while angles on a straight line sum to 180°).

questions.question: When two lines cross, the vertically opposite angles are always:
options: Unequal unless the lines are perpendicular
questions.rationale: Vertically opposite angles formed by two crossing lines are always equal — a core angle-chasing fact derived from straight-line sums.

questions.question: An angle measuring between 180° and 360° is called:
questions.rationale: Reflex angles lie between 180° and 360°; a straight angle is exactly 180° and obtuse angles lie between 90° and 180°.

questions.question: Using the polygon angle-sum pattern $(n-2) \times 180°$, the interior angles of a hexagon (n = 6) sum to:
questions.rationale: (6 − 2) × 180° = 4 × 180° = 720° — this generalisation follows from the triangle's 180° angle sum via parallel-line facts.
